video_title: Bobby Marks' Offseason Guide for the Detroit Pistons 🚨 | NBA on ESPN

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks criticizes Pistons' fan approval after a disappointing playoff exit
quotes.excerpt: I would basically temper your approval rating as far as how this season was for Detroit.
quotes.quote: I understand the crowd cheering for them at the end, but when you lose by 30-plus points at home and you're the number one seed, and although this roster is young and had been to a conference semifinals, then lose two games in a row for the first time all season, I would basically temper your approval rating as far as how this season was for Detroit. Your window, I don't ever want to say window is closed and stuff like that, but windows don't stay open forever. I think we know that for certain in this league.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks outlines Detroit's draft picks and key free agents for the offseason
quotes.excerpt: You've got one pick in the first round, which is from Minnesota, the 21st pick in the draft.
quotes.quote: So where do the Pistons go this offseason here? You've got one pick in the first round, which is from Minnesota that you moved up at the trade deadline here. It's the 21st pick in the draft. You have some key free agents when you look at Jalen Duren, and we're going to talk about him in a minute, who's a restricted free agent, Tobias Harris, Javonte Green. Danis Jenkins has got a team option. You have all your picks moving forward, so you can trade those in the future. You have four first-round picks if you wanted to move 2027, 2029, 2031, and 2033. You can do that, so you basically have up to five first. You've got pick swaps, you've got some future seconds.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks reflects on Detroit's roster building, patience, and recent player acquisitions
quotes.excerpt: Sometimes roster building is a cruel reminder that patience always is not rewarded.
quotes.quote: The biggest thing for me is that sometimes roster building is a cruel reminder that patience always is not rewarded. So when you look at Detroit after losing to New York last year in the first round, they went out and got Duncan Robinson in a sign and trade and Caris LeVert and made some trimming around the edges type moves. You brought back Paul Reed, who was actually really good for you. And at the trade deadline you traded for Kevin Huerter, who was hurt most of these playoffs and really didn't do much for you. Of course, Danis Jenkins was a great find, you convert him to a regular contract off a two-way, you traded Jaden Ivey. But when you looked at Game 7, Game 5 at the end, certainly from a scoring standpoint, like I know you never want to play Monday morning quarterback, but goodness gracious, could you imagine like Coby White or Ayo Dosunmu on this Detroit roster in this series, especially Game 5? Game 7 was a once it got down to 10 and I said it, it was like basically it was like a 20-point lead.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks analyzes Jalen Duren's declining contract value due to poor playoff performance
quotes.excerpt: The biggest thing is going to be what happens with Jalen Duren, who I thought was on pace to potentially sign a max contract.
quotes.quote: The biggest thing is going to be what happens with Jalen Duren, who I thought was on pace to potentially sign a max contract, which would have been five for I think 238, 239. If he reaches, if he's named All-NBA this for this year, which I think he has a good chance, which would be certainly ironic, he would then be eligible to sign a five-year, I believe the number is five for 239 and five for 287 is the number if he earns All-NBA. That's not automatically kick in because it's not an extension, it's a rookie contract. It basically has to be negotiated, which I would certainly think you're not going to sign Duren for five for 287. I don't think he's at five for 239. I think his number has gone down considerably. Restricted free agency is a bear. Cap space, cap space, cap space, you've got to have a team out there to make an offer. Last center that signed a max deal was Deandre Ayton and that's because Indiana came in with an offer sheet. We know how much the production of Duren has dropped. It's the second worst point differential from the regular season to the postseason in NBA history. And I had thought in Game 6 he had turned a corner, I think he went 15 and 11, and then in Game 7, it was like we're back to the, basically got bullied by Mobley and Jarrett Allen here.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks discusses Tobias Harris's inconsistent playoff performance and free agency outlook
quotes.excerpt: He had been really, really good up until I guess Game 5. Then the wheels fell off with him.
quotes.quote: Then you've got Tobias Harris as far as what to figure out. He had been really, really good up until I guess Game 5. Eight games of at least 20 points or more, 30 points in that Game 7 win against Orlando, and then man, the wheels fell off with him. Fewer than 20 points in Game 6 and Game 7, he scored less than 10 points. Four games against Cleveland, less than 20 points. He is an early bird, you can bring him back, you can exceed the cap. We'll show their finances in a minute. But you have a decision as far as what the free agent class is not good. I will just say this, like I just I'm writing an article for Friday, it is a bad, not a bad group, it's just an old group. It's an old group and Tobias is probably one of the top 10 unrestricted free agents out there. Rui Hachimura, another name out there, you could have the non-tax mid-level for him potentially if you don't bring Tobias back here.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks explains Detroit's financial situation, highlighting Jalen Duren's cap hold and its impact
quotes.excerpt: When you add the Duren cap hold, you're basically right at the salary cap.
quotes.quote: Here's Robinson, $2 million guaranteed. Here's Paul Reed, non-guaranteed. Here are your team options. Here is Jalen Duren, he's got a $19 million cap hold. So you're at roughly $139 million. When you add the Duren cap hold, you're basically right at the salary cap. The only way that you could become a cap space team and still retain Duren is basically you waive, waive, waive, so you're basically diminishing your depth and you're getting, you're creating $30-plus million in depth. You've got that pick there. So that is where you are financially here. As I said, you're really in good shape, you're $62 million under the tax, but the cap hold counts against the cap. That is why we have them as a projected over the cap team here.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks evaluates Ausar Thompson's extension eligibility, noting his offensive limitations
quotes.excerpt: Offensively sometimes it's like playing four-on-five, and that is a struggle.
quotes.quote: You have a decision with Ausar Thompson, he is another tough one to peg as far as he is extension eligible this offseason here. I don't see him, listen, he'll make All-Defensive team. I don't see him as a max player. I just can't. I mean the two of them, the two brothers, him and Amen, I just, I mean offensively sometimes it's like playing four-on-five, and that is a struggle. So I think his number for me, it would be roughly north of $16-17 million of the cap, which would be $26-27 million. I think whatever the percentage of Jaden McDaniels was in Minnesota, that is kind of how I see him. And then you've got Isaiah Stewart, Marcus Sasser, who's also rookie extension, and Kevin Huerter.
